chain.title: Menril Log
chain.desc: Cut down a Menril tree - the tall blue-white trees that generate across the Overworld and densely in the Meneglin biome. Everything in this mod starts here.

chain.title: Menril Berries
chain.desc: Harvested from Menril leaves. Eating them clears every bad potion effect, and they are the light source inside display panels.

chain.title: Squeezer
chain.desc: Iron ingots, an iron block, planks and a stick. Drop a Menril log in, right-click the piston down, and it wrings out Menril Resin.

chain.title: Drying Basin
chain.desc: Logs, iron and black dye. Pour Menril Resin in and let it evaporate; the residue is a Crystalized Menril Block.

chain.title: Crystalized Menril Block
chain.desc: The dried output of the basin. Log to resin to block is the whole resource loop, and it is worth automating before you build anything else.

chain.title: Crystalized Menril Chunk
chain.desc: Break the block into nine chunks. This is the currency of the mod - almost every part, cable and machine has a chunk in its recipe.

chain.title: On the Dynamics of Integration
chain.desc: A book and a chunk. The in-game manual, and genuinely the fastest way to understand what a variable card actually is.

chain.title: Logic Cable
chain.desc: Sticks, redstone and chunks. Cables carry the network; parts clip onto their faces, and a network is just the set of cables touching each other.

chain.title: Wrench
chain.desc: Chunks and redstone. It pops parts off cables and rotates them without breaking the network you have already run.

chain.title: Logic Programmer
chain.desc: A crafting table and a Crystalized Menril Block. This is where you actually write logic: pick operators, feed them variables, and get a new variable card out.

chain.title: Variable Card
chain.desc: Paper and a chunk. A blank card. Everything the network computes is written onto one of these in the Logic Programmer.

chain.title: Variable Store
chain.desc: A wooden chest, a Crystalized Menril Block and chunks. Cards only exist to the network while they sit in a store attached to it.

chain.title: Input Variable Transformer
chain.desc: A sticky piston, a chunk and a Variable Card. The reader half of every part - if a part reads the world, this is inside it.

chain.title: Output Variable Transformer
chain.desc: The same with a plain piston. The writer half; every part that acts on the world is built from one of these.

chain.title: Inventory Reader
chain.desc: A wooden chest and an Input Transformer. Clip it to a cable against a chest and the network can see stack counts, slots and contents as values.

chain.title: Redstone Writer
chain.desc: Redstone dust, a redstone block and an Output Transformer. Feed it a boolean or an integer and it emits the signal - the simplest way to make logic do something.

chain.title: Static Light Panel
chain.desc: Menril Berries, redstone and an Output Transformer; a lit blank face on a cable, and the base of the display panel.

chain.title: Display Panel
chain.desc: Berries and an Output Transformer on a Static Light Panel. Point a variable at it and it prints the live value on the wall - your debugger.

chain.title: Proxy
chain.desc: Iron, planks, a Variable Card and a Variable Store. It gives one variable a network-wide name so a dozen parts can reference the same computed value.

chain.title: Materializer
chain.desc: Obsidian, diamond, redstone and a Variable Card. It freezes a live computed value into a literal card, which is how you break feedback loops.

chain.title: Delay
chain.desc: A clock, chunks, a Variable Card and a Variable Store. It remembers a value's history, giving the network the one thing pure logic cannot do: state over time.

chain.title: Energy Battery
chain.desc: A redstone block, a Crystalized Menril Block and chunks. Parts run on energy once you scale up, and batteries combine into larger ones in the grid.

chain.title: Coal Generator
chain.desc: Shapeless from a furnace and an Energy Battery. Crude, but enough to keep a wall of writers and the mechanical machines ticking.

chain.title: Mechanical Squeezer
chain.desc: A Squeezer, an Energy Battery, obsidian and diamonds. It does the same job on RF instead of right-clicks, and gets you off the manual resin loop.

chain.title: Proto Chorus
chain.desc: Menril Berries and an ender pearl. Squeeze it for Liquid Chorus, and dry that for Crystalized Chorus - the second, End-flavoured resource line.

chain.title: Logic Director
chain.desc: Diamonds, a Crystalized Menril Chunk and a Crystalized Chorus Chunk. It rewrites variable cards inside a store automatically, so the network can reprogram itself.

chain.title: Omni-Directional Connector
chain.desc: Built by a dedicated recipe serializer rather than a plain shaped recipe: connectors are made and paired in groups, and a matched pair welds two distant networks into one across any distance.

notes: THE PARTS ARE THE MOD, AND A NAIVE ID PASS LOSES ALL 21 OF THEM. Strict models INTERSECT lang finds 59 ids; the 21 integrateddynamics:part_* items have item models but NO item.integrateddynamics.* or block.integrateddynamics.* lang key. They are named under an INVERTED CONVENTION: parttype.integrateddynamics.<name> (e.g. parttype.integrateddynamics.inventory_reader = 'Inventory Reader', with a matching .info key). WIDENED TO 80 ON THAT PROOF - item model + parttype lang key + a shaped recipe for 20 of the 21. Pass 2 re-derived the whole set independently from .class constant-pool strings, item textures, blockstates, recipe results and loot tables and corroborated every one of the 80; the only two things pass 2 surfaced that pass 1 had not claimed were menril_torch_wall and menril_torch_stone_wall, which are wall-mounted torch blockstates with no item form (exactly like minecraft:wall_torch) and are correctly excluded. A SECOND RECIPE MISS, REGISTERED IN CODE: part_connector_omni_directional is the one part with no ordinary recipe result. It is produced by three custom serializers - integrateddynamics:crafting_special_shaped_omni_directional, _shaped_omni_directional_3 and _shapeless_omni_directional - whose recipe JSONs carry a type and nothing else, with the shape and result in RecipeSerializerCraftingSpecialShapedOmniDirectionalConfig.class. It IS obtainable; a result-key scan would have wrongly dropped it, so its chain description names the mechanic (paired connectors) rather than a shape the jar does not contain. THE RESOURCE LOOP IS NOT A CRAFTING RECIPE. crystalized_menril_block has no grid recipe: it comes from an integrateddynamics:drying_basin / mechanical_drying_basin recipe consuming 1000mB of integrateddynamics:menril_resin, and that fluid comes from an integrateddynamics:squeezer / mechanical_squeezer recipe on a menril_log (1000mB) or menril_planks (250mB). The chorus line is the same shape: popped_chorus_fruit or proto_chorus -> liquid_chorus -> crystalized_chorus_block. Both machines are therefore hard prerequisites for every other item in the mod, which is why they sit at steps 3 and 4. WORLDGEN IS THE ENTRY POINT: data/integrateddynamics/worldgen/biome/meneglin.json defines the Meneglin biome and data/integrateddynamics/forge/biome_modifier/add_feature_menril_overworld.json injects tree_menril_general into the wider Overworld, so menril_log, menril_leaves, menril_sapling, menril_berries and menril_log_filled are all worldgen-sourced with block loot tables and no recipe - obtainable, correctly kept. DROPPED AS UNOBTAINABLE: integrateddynamics:energy_battery_creative (creative-only; no recipe) and integrateddynamics:invisible_light (a technical light-source block with no recipe and no loot table). Also excluded from the chain per the desirability rule: the crystalized menril/chorus block and brick slabs and stairs, menril_slab, menril_planks_stairs, and the stripped menril log and wood variants - the block and brick forms carry the family in a wheel instead. integrateddynamics:variable_transformer is a lang-only grouping key ('Input/Output Variable Transformers'), not a registered item; the two real transformers are in the chain. NO CONSENSUS DATA: moddb.json has no integrateddynamics entry, so ordering is the recipe dependency graph alone. Jar confirmed 1.20.1 Forge: META-INF/mods.toml with modIds integrateddynamics + bundled integrateddynamicscompat (which registers no items of its own), minecraft versionRange [1.20.1,], pack_format 15, Java 17 class files, no fabric.mod.json; Modrinth lists this exact file under game_versions ['1.20.1'] and loaders ['forge']. Hard dependencies on cyclopscore and commoncapabilities must be present for any of this to load.
